about_the_game:
The game is being developed by one person, and there may be bugs and inaccuracies. The work in progress shown here does not reflect the final look of the game.

Do you dream of eternal life? Is it better than death? If life is eternal, then absolutely any event that can be imagined will happen in its endless course. All the nightmares, horrors, and abominations imaginable are bound to happen. This means that one day you will experience the events of this game in reality. So which is better: eternal life or eternal oblivion?

Imagine: You've spent eternity in a small, cramped room, never seeing anything outside the cold, unnatural walls. How long have you been here? A century? A millennium? Maybe even more. You don't know how or why you ended up here, and the only memory of another life is a green forest, a noisy river, and fresh air, which seem like an illusion of mind that helps you stay sane.

There is only one way out: a massive rusty door, presumably opening with a lever on the side of the wall. But the thought of opening a passage causes you an irresistible, inexplicable horror. The house loves you, feeds you with the nutrient mass that periodically appears on the floor, and even turns on the water in a rusty shower in a raw bathroom. The house doesn't want to let you go, and you don't want to leave it.

Recently, strange noises were heard outside, pipes began to groan, and the walls seemed to be narrowing. In addition, a bleeding tumor has appeared on your emaciated, thin body, causing unbearable pain and increasing every day. The crazy, meaningless world began to crumble. Although you are tired, you still have a crazy desire for life in your mind. Is there a way to prevent the end? There is no way out — with great effort you open a door that has been locked for thousands of years.

The laws of this world defy explanation. Rooms shift in a nonsensical, chaotic order, as if they are a random assortment of elements from a previously existing world. Like the surrounding environment, the creature outside is a pure manifestation of madness. It is far stronger and faster than you, with perfect hearing and an acute sense of smell.

Simply running away or hiding won't work. To survive, you must not only avoid encounters with the creature but also deceive its senses, confusing it with your scent and other signs of presence. Set traps, plan every action and strategy down to the smallest detail. Your greatest ally is a clear mind.

  • Realistic physics allows you to interact with the environment, opening up new possibilities for passing. Place boxes on top of each other to climb over obstacles, climb cabinets, or use objects to distract the Creature. Yours survival depends not only on the ability to hide, but also on a creative approach to solving problems.

  • Create traps, auxiliary devices, and mix chemicals. The further you advance, the more items you will have at your disposal, opening up new possibilities for survival strategies. New items will be systematically added during the development process.

  • Explore crazy locations, look for useful items that make it easier to complete, items for your crafts, tools to overcome obstacles, and more. Each item you find expands your options for survival and strategic planning.

  • After all, don't forget to give your exhausted body and mind a chance to relax. Lock the door in one of the Safe rooms, each with its own unique atmosphere. While there, enjoy the calm music and a pleasant feeling of security. Most likely, no one will bother you here.

content_descriptors.notes: As a horror title, The Tumor features blood, gore, and scenes that many users may find discomforting or gross. All violence is presented in a heavily stylized, pixelated/low-poly format.

short_description: Hardcore stealth survival-horror in retro style with realistic physics. The creature is faster, hears, and feels you perfectly. Escape is impossible. Craft, set traps, strategize. Hide, deceive, and fight to uncover the truth.
